name: MARQUISE (SOLITAIRE)
description: Marquise (often associated with the Marquise de Pompadour) is an elegant, historical French solitaire game played with a 32-card piquet deck. It is a game of patience and careful sequence building, reflecting the aristocratic pastimes of the 18th-century French court. Unlike modern Klondike, it is a tighter, more deterministic puzzle due to the smaller deck size and specific building constraints.

content.text: Marquise (often associated with the Marquise de Pompadour) is an elegant, historical French solitaire game played with a 32-card piquet deck. It is a game of patience and careful sequence building, reflecting the aristocratic pastimes of the 18th-century French court. Unlike modern Klondike, it is a tighter, more deterministic puzzle due to the smaller deck size and specific building constraints.
Dates to the mid-18th century. Popular legend attributes its refinement to Madame de Pompadour, the chief mistress of Louis XV, during her time at Versailles.
One player only. Marquise is a solitaire (patience) game for a single player; the player works against the layout, building four foundation piles by suit and managing the tableau and stock.
Deal according to solitaire layout; reserve and tableau as per rules.
